# The read-back

New goal’s last step reads the goal back in sentences, with what was left as usual and what you said, then says what happens after it is published: when the first check-in is due, who sees it, the reviews it joins and how long it can be taken back.

## The rule

**The rows** (rule 5, `readBack`), each a small label, a sentence and Change to its step; after Change, Continue comes straight back, and a change that leaves a later step needing something (another type) opens that step first.

- **What**: a number to move, “A number to move: from 40% in week 46 (9–15 Nov 2026) to 90% by week 53 (28 Dec 2026–3 Jan 2027), the same amount each week. Higher is better.” (the shape: “the same amount each week”, “slowly at first, faster near the end”, “in a few jumps”, or “with the weeks’ numbers set by hand”; weeks as [years and weeks](years-and-weeks.md) says them); a range, “A number to keep in range: at or under 12%. It warns only once the limit is crossed.” (or “It warns within 1% of the limit.”); stages, “Dated stages: 2 stages, the last due week 50 (7–13 Dec 2026).” then how many are already done or overdue ([a goal not born late](not-born-late.md)).
- **Who and where**: “{Owner} owns it, in {team}. It’s a Team goal and feeds “{parent}” ({key}).”, or “… and feeds nothing: it’s at the top of its own tree.”; then what else it helps, and “It’s a guardrail.”
- **Measured by** (number goals): the metric chosen (“Lead time for changes, for CI/CD.”), or “No metric: “{how it’s measured}”.”, or “No metric, and not described yet.”
- **Left as usual** (`leftAsUsual`): every default not changed, judged by value, in this order: “Whole numbers.”, “From this week to the end of 2026.”, “Steady.”, “No early warning.”, “Not a guardrail.”, “Helps no other goal.” Change goes to the first one’s step. Absent when nothing was left. (Feeding nothing is said once, in Who and where.)
- **You said**: each answered question’s read-back sentence ([goal entry](goal-entry.md), rule 3), with no Change. Absent when none.

**After you publish.** With the weekly rhythm: “Its first check-in is due by Thursday 12 Nov, then every week.” (the first review day on or after today, `firstReview`, or From’s week when the plan starts later), then for a number to move “The first number sets where it stands; the plan says 47% for week 47.” (the plan for the week after this one), for a range “It asks for this week’s number.”, for stages “It asks which stages are done.” With no rhythm: “It shows as “No check-in yet” until you post its first number. Nothing is due.” Stages that are all already done: “Every stage is already done, so no check-in is due.” Then who sees it (“Everyone in {workspace} can see it.”, or for someone else “{Owner} sees it on their Home the next time they open Faro. Faro doesn’t send email.”); with Reviews on, the reviews that will walk it (`reviewsJoining`: `goalsIn` applied to the goal as built; “It joins Platform leadership weekly, which walks every north star.”, several by name, or “It joins no review yet.”); and how long it can be taken back (“Until its first check-in you can change anything, or delete it. After that, a change to the plan needs a reason.”, or for someone else “Only {owner} or an admin can change it once it is published. …”). Stages already done are saved as its first check-in, so then: “Its stage already done is its first check-in, so it can be stopped, with a reason, but not deleted. A change to the plan needs a reason.”

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Tunde’s “Signed artifacts in staging”, 40% → 90% by week 53, steady, Team, feeds G-41; on Wednesday 11 Nov 2026 (week 46, due Thursday). | `A number to move: from 40% in week 46 (9–15 Nov 2026) to 90% by week 53 (28 Dec 2026–3 Jan 2027), the same amount each week. Higher is better. / Its first check-in is due by Thursday 12 Nov, then every week. The first number sets where it stands; the plan says 47% for week 47.` |
| The same, published on Friday 13 Nov. | `Its first check-in is due by Thursday 19 Nov, then every week. The first number sets where it stands; the plan says 47% for week 47.` |
| The same, with no rhythm. | `It shows as “No check-in yet” until you post its first number. Nothing is due.` |
| Owned by Amara, added by someone else. | `Amara sees it on their Home the next time they open Faro. Faro doesn’t send email.` |
| A north star, with the demo’s reviews; then with Reviews off. | `It joins Platform leadership weekly and Quarterly business review. / no review line` |
| A range at most 12%, no margin; one stage due week 50. | `A number to keep in range: at or under 12%. It warns only once the limit is crossed. / Dated stages: 1 stage, the last due week 50 (7–13 Dec 2026).` |
| Left as usual for a goal that feeds nothing; nothing defaulted. | `Whole numbers. From this week to the end of 2026. Steady. Not a guardrail. Helps no other goal. / no row` |
| Stages, one of two already done. | `Its stage already done is its first check-in, so it can be stopped, with a reason, but not deleted. A change to the plan needs a reason.` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The rhythm and Reviews switches (FT1, FT2) are not built yet: New goal reads back the weekly rhythm with Reviews on. Pronouns aren’t kept, so someone else’s Home is “their Home”.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/readBack.ts](../../../src/domain/readBack.ts): `readBack`, `leftAsUsual`, `reviewsJoining`
- [src/domain/progress.ts](../../../src/domain/progress.ts): `firstReview`, `reviewDate`
- [src/domain/review.ts](../../../src/domain/review.ts): `goalsIn`

## Requirements

- `NEW-GOAL-STEPS`: New goal asks what, who and where, how it's measured, then reads it back in sentences, with what was left as usual and what happens after it is published; each step has an address and nothing is chosen from a list of everything.
- `GOAL-ENTRY-REQUIRED`: Every way of adding a goal says what it needs before it is refused, checks it with one rule, and asks rather than assumes where a value is possible but unlikely; nothing is saved before it has been read back.

## Tests that check it

### [src/domain/readBack.test.ts](../../../src/domain/readBack.test.ts)

- the read-back (rule 5) › reads a number to move back with its weeks, and when its first check-in is due (Wednesday 11 Nov)
- the read-back (rule 5) › published on Friday 13 Nov, it is due the Thursday after
- the read-back (rule 5) › with no rhythm, nothing is due and no weekday is named
- the read-back (rule 5) › for someone else, says who sees it and who can change it
- the read-back (rule 5) › names the review it joins, and with Reviews off has no review line
- the read-back (rule 5) › a range at most 12%, no margin; and with one
- the read-back (rule 5) › one stage due week 50 is “1 stage”, never “1 stages”
- the read-back (rule 5) › says every default not changed, and Change goes to the first; nothing defaulted, no row
- the read-back (rule 5) › Measured by: the metric, a description or neither; You said: each answer
- the read-back (rule 5) › a stage already done is a check-in: the goal can be stopped, not deleted (build review of #202, finding 4)
- the read-back (rule 5) › with every stage done, nothing is due (build review of #202, a low)
- the read-back (rule 5) › a north star feeds nothing: the top of its own tree
- reviewsJoining › a level, a tree, neither, and an ended review
